compiled:
📰 General

Rod Wave’s Grammy Hope Dashed as He’s Arrested on Gun & Drug Charges •

Rapper Rod Wave was arrested in Atlanta on Wednesday, the same day he received his first Grammy nomination. The 27-year-old, whose real name is Rodarius Green, was booked on four charges related to firearms and narcotics. Law enforcement officials have not yet released specific details regarding the charges or the circumstances of the arrest. The arrest occurred just hours after Rod Wave’s recognition by the Recording Academy.

🌍 World

Goldin Family Awaits Confirmation as Hamas Claims Location of Remains •

The Goldin family issued a statement Saturday evening following Hamas’s assertion of locating the body of Lt. Hadar Goldin within a tunnel in the Rafah area. The family expressed their anticipation for official confirmation of the discovery. Hamas representatives stated they believed they had identified Goldin’s remains, though verification remains pending. This development follows weeks of intense searching and negotiations regarding the retrieval of remains of hostages held in Gaza.

🦅 US

FAA-Ordered Flight Cancellations Set to Surge as Government Shutdown Lingers •

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is preparing for a significant increase in flight cancellations next week due to the ongoing government shutdown. Airlines have been instructed to reduce their operations by hundreds of flights as a result of staffing shortages within the FAA. This marks the longest government shutdown in U.S. history, impacting air traffic control and creating widespread operational disruptions. The FAA is prioritizing essential flights while attempting to mitigate the cascading effects of the shutdown.

💰 Business

Millionaires Favor Personal Trainers Over Wealth Advisors, Survey Reveals •

A recent survey indicates a shift in spending priorities among high-net-worth individuals. Millionaires are expressing dissatisfaction with traditional wealth advisors and accountants. Interestingly, a significant portion of this group is investing heavily in personal trainers and therapists. The study highlights a growing demand for wellness and personal development services compared to traditional financial management.

💻 Technology

New amiibo Lineup Announced: Mario Galaxy, Kirby Air Riders, and Resident Evil Confirmed •

Nintendo has unveiled a substantial lineup of amiibo figures slated for release between 2025 and 2026, continuing the series’ longevity. The upcoming collection includes figures based on Super Mario Galaxy, Kirby and the Air Racers, and Resident Evil, expanding the range of available characters. Pre-orders for these figures are expected to begin soon, though specific dates and pricing have not yet been released. This expansion demonstrates continued support for the amiibo system and its diverse range of licensed properties.

🎭 Entertainment

Predator: Badlands Delivers Record-Breaking Box Office Opening Weekend •

Predator: Badlands, directed by Dan Trachtenberg, achieved a significant opening weekend at the domestic box office. The film grossed $15.6 million on Friday, leading the charts and setting it on track for a record-breaking opening. This performance marks a welcome return to success for the action genre after a recent period of lower box office returns. Industry analysts predict the film will surpass $36 million in its opening weekend.

🏅 Sports

Oregon Ducks Secure 18-16 Road Victory Over No. 20 Iowa Hawkeyes •

The No. 9 Oregon Ducks defeated the No. 20 Iowa Hawkeyes 18-16 in a hard-fought contest at Kinnick Stadium. Quarterback Dante Moore spearheaded the Ducks’ offense, leading a crucial drive in the fourth quarter to tie the game. Oregon ultimately secured the victory after a defensive stop and a successful field goal. The win marked the Ducks’ eleventh consecutive road victory.

🔬 Science

NASA’s EscaPADE Mission Prepares for Unprecedented Journey to Uncover Martian Atmospheric Loss •

NASA’s EscaPADE mission, utilizing twin spacecraft, is scheduled for launch to investigate the long-term atmospheric loss of Mars. The mission will employ an unconventional, winding orbital trajectory to study the planet’s history. Scientists aim to determine the factors responsible for the significant reduction in Mars’ atmosphere over billions of years. Data collected will contribute to understanding planetary evolution and habitability. The project represents a novel approach to studying the Red Planet’s past.

🩺 Health

Pioneer of Life-Support Technology, Robert H. Bartlett, Passes Away at 86 •

Robert H. Bartlett, a surgeon instrumental in developing the Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO) system, died at his home in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Bartlett’s work led to the creation of ECMO, a critical technology that provides temporary support for a patient’s heart and lungs during severe illness or injury. The system functions by diverting blood outside the body to deliver oxygen and remove carbon dioxide. Bartlett’s innovation has saved countless lives and remains a cornerstone of intensive care medicine.
